frontier_selection.reason: Fresh swarm refresh showed active parallel lanes for ClayCode, loop-core/GWT, UnifiedDB, Retina, token API, effect authority, web ingress, reward and capability/body. PR #337 had a target-green V3 SQLite admission repair with one explicit remaining product boundary: trusted product boot/service wiring must establish the isolated interpreter before import-capable Frank code.

fresh_external_evidence.finding: -I implies -E, -P and -s; -S is a separate option disabling site import and site-dependent sys.path manipulations.
Executable import lines in .pth files are processed by site and run at Python startup when that site path is processed.
Type=exec reports failure when execve of the configured service binary cannot be performed, making it preferable to Type=simple for a trusted launcher composition.
3.53.4 includes the WAL-reset database corruption fix already selected by the storage lane.

hypothesis: The V3 trusted Python -I startup boundary prevents site-path executable code from running before V3 admission.
strongest_counterhypothesis: -I does not disable site initialization, so an executable .pth import line can run before V3 main; the trusted launcher must also supply -S.

go_oob.safety: Disposable Python virtual environment and marker file only; no Frank database, external provider effect, host package replacement, training action or Harness mutation.

local_execution.baseline: venv Python -I processed an executable .pth line before main and wrote the marker
local_execution.rescue: the same interpreter with -I -S did not execute the .pth payload

target_vps_execution.step: Execute the single GO OOB and same-discriminator V4 repair regression

go_oob.counterevidence_status: No evidence found that -I itself implies -S; official Python 3.12 documentation explicitly separates the flags.

target_repo_delta.candidate_change: V4 requires isolated+ignore_environment+safe_path+no_user_site+no_site, preserves -I -S across child execve, and retains V1/V2/V3 SQLite/loader/module-origin checks.

architecture_delta.change: Treat Python site initialization as part of the trusted pre-Frank launch boundary. Require -I -S before any import-capable Frank Python code in the storage/state process, then preserve the flags through admission re-exec.
architecture_delta.expected_effect: Closes the reproduced executable-.pth pre-guard startup path while preserving the fixed private SQLite admission chain.
architecture_delta.strongest_counterhypothesis: The extra no-site constraint may be unnecessary in a fully immutable trusted Python installation or may break required site-provided dependencies; real product service wiring and actual production dependency composition must measure this rather than assume it.
architecture_delta.rollback: Drop PR #342 / V4 candidate and retain V3 with the negative result recorded; no canonical target state was changed.

negative_results.claim_refuted: V3 -I alone is a complete Python startup trust boundary against site-path startup code
negative_results.scope: Reproduced locally and on the accepted target VPS workflow lane

remaining_falsifiers: Verify real product service/deployment wiring launches the exact admitted interpreter with -I -S before any import-capable Frank Python code.
Bind accepted source/binary/private-SQLite manifest identities and fail closed on service drift.
Measure whether -S removes any dependency required by the real production token API/runtime; do not infer from candidate gates or disposable pair smoke.
Revalidate the same startup boundary on the final Andreas Ubuntu target system before release acceptance.

research_reentry.next_frontier: Retain V3 as insufficient negative evidence and V4 as the target-supported repair successor candidate. The next useful non-OOB frontier is real product systemd/deployment launch composition: exact admitted Python executable, -I -S before import-capable Frank code, accepted source/binary/private-SQLite manifest identities, fail-closed drift detection, and production dependency compatibility under -S.
